policies.title: Dutch ordinary passports: Burkina Faso electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: Netherlands guidance expressly directs a Dutch passport holder who needs a Burkina Faso visa to Visa Burkina, whose official procedure confirms electronic visa issuance.
conditions: Use an ordinary Dutch passport and complete the electronic application and payment before travel. This is electronic issuance, not the separate travel form or an arrival visa.
Embassy, migration-service, residence, work, transit, special-document, carrier and final-admission conditions remain separate.

policies.title: Dutch ordinary passports: Côte d’Ivoire preapproved arrival visitor visa
policies.summary: Netherlands guidance directs Dutch passport holders requiring a Côte d’Ivoire visa to SNEDAI; its official process requires online pre-enrolment then prints and issues the visa at Abidjan airport.
conditions: Use a valid ordinary Dutch passport. Complete SNEDAI pre-enrolment, payment and required documents, receive the approved response, and carry it when boarding.

The visa is printed and issued after biometric enrolment at Abidjan airport. This is preapproved border issuance, not an eVisa. ECOWAS, residence, work, transit, diplomatic or other special-document routes remain separate.

policies.title: Dutch ordinary passports: Jordan arrival visitor visa
policies.summary: Netherlands guidance expressly says a Dutch-passport holder can buy a Jordan visa at the airport or a Jordanian border office.
conditions: Use an ordinary Dutch passport valid for at least six months on arrival. The online Ministry of Interior E-visa is an alternative route and does not alter the stated arrival-issuance baseline.
Jordan Pass, group tourism, transit, Hajj, diplomatic passports, residence, extensions, carrier checks and final admission remain separate.

conflicts.explanation: The current recognised SNEDAI procedure requires pre-enrolment before travel but prints and issues the visa only after biometric enrolment at Abidjan airport.
